definitions: A central pattern in Domain-Driven Design. It is a logical boundary around a specific part of a larger system, within which a particular domain model is defined and consistent.
A linguistic and semantic boundary that encapsulates a specific model, ensuring its consistency and preventing ambiguity with other models in a larger software system.
examples: Each bounded context should have its own ubiquitous language.
The team decided to split the application into several bounded contexts.
Defining the bounded context clearly is crucial for microservices architecture.
